name: Hertfordshire
description: Hertfordshire is an affluent county immediately north of London, characterised by attractive countryside, commuter towns and historic market centres. Places such as St Albans, Watford and Hertford have strong connections to London, while the county also hosts significant business and technology industries.

places.name: Dacorum
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire covering the New Town of Hemel Hempstead and the historic canal town of Berkhamsted, with its Norman castle ruins.

places.name: Welwyn Hatfield
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire home to Welwyn Garden City, one of Britain's pioneering planned garden cities from the early 20th century, alongside the historic town of Hatfield.

places.name: Three Rivers
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire named for the Chess, Colne, and Gade rivers, covering the town of Rickmansworth and access to the Chiltern Hills.

places.name: Broxbourne
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire along the Lee Valley, covering the towns of Cheshunt and Hoddesdon on London's northern commuter fringe.

places.name: East Hertfordshire
places.description: A rural district covering the market towns of Hertford and Bishop's Stortford, with countryside stretching toward the Essex border.

places.name: Hertsmere
places.description: A district in Hertfordshire home to Elstree Studios, a historic British film and TV production hub, and the town of Borehamwood.

places.name: North Hertfordshire
places.description: A district covering the historic market town of Hitchin and the garden city of Letchworth, the world's first, planned in 1903.

places.name: St Albans
places.description: A cathedral city in Hertfordshire built on the site of the Roman city of Verulamium, with an abbey marking the martyrdom of Britain's first Christian saint.

places.name: Stevenage
places.description: One of Britain's first post-war New Towns, built in Hertfordshire from 1946 as a model for pedestrian-friendly urban planning.

places.name: Watford
places.description: A commuter town in Hertfordshire on the edge of London, historically a printing and brewing centre, now known for its large shopping centre and football club.
